messages:
laura: Heads-up — I profiled continuous-batching in prod this morning and noticed repeated kernel-switch spikes whenever KV cache hit-rate falls below ~65%. Want to get a focused telemetry dashboard that ties batch_utilization, queue_depth, tokens/sec, kv_cache_hit_rate and kernel_switch_rate so we can detect and auto-adjust batch formation / token budgets. Can we sync on what panels + alerts to add?

arjun: Can you drop the trace snippet / timestamps so I can correlate with kernel logs?

laura: Pasted the slice (span ids) in the incident gist: https://gists.company/repro-batch-kv-2026 — spikes at ~2026-03-17T09:12:xxZ and 09:18:xxZ. Quick PromQL I used:```
avg by(pool) (batch_utilization{env="prod"})
max by(route) (tokens_per_sec{env="prod"})
avg by(route) (kv_cache_hit_rate{env="prod"})
increase(kernel_switches_total{env="prod"}[5m]) / 5
```
Use those as starting panels.

ben: We have a batch_utilization panel but it's per-GPU-pool only. Need token/sec split by route and kernel id. Kernel id currently high-card (xla/cuda/quant), but we should collect kernel_name tag in the exporter.

sophie: +1. Also add microbatch_size distribution and 95th latency per microbatch. When kv miss forces a fallback kernel we see both utilization drop and latency tail spike. Something like:```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
```
and microbatch size: `sum by(route, size_bin) (increase(microbatch_count[10m]))`

maria: I can sketch panels in Grafana. Question: what concrete alerting rules? Are we paging on this or SLO-only?

laura: Proposal: page if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.6 for 5m AND batch_utilization < 0.3 for 5m AND kernel_switch_rate > 4/min for 5m. Otherwise fire a ticket. Rationale: this combo indicates cache thrash -> kernel fallbacks -> wasted tokens.

arjun: That AND we should include a suppression for planned model rollouts (label rollout=true) to avoid noisy pages. Also, cardinality: rollup by topk(10, route) + sample the rest at 10% to keep panels useful.

ben: For the dashboard UX, add a small table showing top offending routes with columns: route, avg_tokens/sec, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switches/5m, avg_microbatch. Should be sortable and link to flame graphs.

sophie: Would help if the runtime exports kernel_choice histograms and a kv_miss_reason label (cold_load, eviction, mem_pressure). Then we can slice by reason.

laura: I'll open an infra task to add kernel_name and kv_miss_reason to the metrics pipeline + patch the exporter. Also prototyping a dashboard with these panels and a compact 'health signal' panel that computes a single score: `0.5*kv_hit_rate + 0.3*batch_util + 0.2*(1 - normalized_kernel_switch_rate)`. If score < 0.45 -> warn.

maria: Sounds good. I can get a PR ready for the Grafana dashboard (JSON model). Recommend adding a 1-min refresh and a 10m aggregated rollup for long-term trends.

ops-bot: grafana: created dashboard "Batching: kernel & kv health (laura/proto)" (dash/8312)

laura: Thanks! I'll prototype an automated policy that reduces target_token_budget by 20% when the health score is < 0.45 for 10m and kv_hit_rate < 0.6 (can be opt-in per-customer). Will share the RFC. :thumbsup:

arjun: Nice. Also let's add a low-overhead sampling trace when health_score flips so we get a few full traces without cost explosion.

ben: Filed issue RW-4925 to track metrics + dashboard + exporter changes. Assigning to laura/maria/arjun.

sophie: i'll validate on canary next week and run a short stress test targeting kv miss patterns.

laura: Great — thanks all. Sync on Monday 10am PT to review the grafana PR and alert rules.
